canonical_statement: The authors identified low initial heparin bolus, low initial infusion rate, and failure to adjust dosing for patient weight as barriers to rapid therapeutic anticoagulation.
The authors suggested that optimal DVT management requires a heparin nomogram or a weight-based heparin dosing nomogram to improve the speed and consistency of anticoagulation.

The article states that the work was supported by the St. Joseph's Health Care Foundation and notes career/scholar support for Deborah Cook from the Ontario Ministry of Health and St. Joseph's Health Care Foundation.

The article contains an internal terminology inconsistency: the abstract and prose define adequate heparinization as PTT >1.5 times control, whereas the Table 1 footnote states >2.5 times control; the extracted attainment results retain the abstract/prose definition and flag the footnote conflict.
